checks.statement_fidelity: The headline is `GX.antoineNecklace_wild_not_isSLSCInCC : IsWildCantor antoineNecklace ∧ ¬ IsSLSCInCC antoineNecklaceᶜ`. `IsSLSCInCC` is the strict library's DEC-55 literal compact-open form (GX/Branched/Galois.lean:959), and the homotopy form implies it, so its negation is the strongest form. `Sphere3` is the unit sphere of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) with the subspace topology. `IsCantorSubset C := Nonempty (C ≃ₜ cantorSet)` is literal. `IsWildCantor C` says C is Cantor and no self-homeomorphism of S³ carries C INTO the great circle {w₂ = w₃ = 0}. This is at least classical wildness, and `GX.antoineNecklace_not_tame` proves the classical form too: not ambient-homeomorphic to `standardCantor3`. `antoineNecklace` is the stereographic image of ⋂ₙ antoineStage n (64 maps of ratio 7/80 iterated on a square solid torus), proved a Cantor set through Fin 64^ℕ ≃ₜ Bool^ℕ. The headline depends only on these definitions. The internal Props (AntoineMeridianEssentialTop, AntoineFirstGeneration, AntoineChainEssential) are all PROVED, so none of them is a hidden assumption. They are also not vacuous: AntoineChainEssential says that for every a ≠ 0 the a-th power of the meridian is not null-homotopic in S³ ∖ stereo(C₁), a satisfiable and non-trivial claim. Under DEC-58/DEC-68 (f), the paper's general 'if S is a wild Cantor set' is read as the one explicit necklace. DEC-82 is met: wildness is certified unconditionally. DEC-85 is met: Antoine's lemma is built, from a topological SvK (the gluing half plus injectivity into Monoid.PushoutI) and a double-cover winding invariant at the first generation. DEC-27 then allows CLOSED under an accepted reading. No extra hypothesis is added. The paper gives this example no proof, so there is nothing further to match.
